name: Confluence
tagline: Collaborative pages, spaces, templates, and organizational knowledge

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 10 users; 2 GB storage; unlimited spaces and pages.
pricing.billingTerms: Standard/Premium monthly + annual; monthly prices are progressive by user count and annual pricing uses fixed user tiers; Enterprise annual only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Invited users count toward billing even before accepting; annual fixed user tiers can make unused capacity billable; Marketplace apps, Atlassian Guard outside Enterprise, and taxes can add cost.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Confluence's durable value is collaboration, integrations, polish, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a single-user team documentation workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: Confluence: Teams pay because shared state, notifications, permissions, and migrations are harder than the visible board or list.
ongoingBurden: Maintain notifications, recurring-date logic, importers, permissions, backups, and collaboration conflict handling.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Open-source task manager with lists, boards, and collaboration.

alternatives.name: XWiki
alternatives.desc: Confluence's grown-up open-source cousin; powerful enough to require an actual administrator

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack, Debian package, or Java application-server distribution
facts.dataFormat: Wiki documents, objects, users, metadata, and usually attachments in a relational database; configuration, extensions, caches, and optional attachment files in the permanent directory
facts.gapVsPaid: It can approach Confluence's depth, but doing so carries a much heavier Java/Solr/database administration burden and less seamless Atlassian ecosystem integration.
facts.setupBlocker: The production setup is a heavyweight Java service with a database, permanent storage, Solr, backups, and TLS to administer

alternatives.name: Docmost
alternatives.desc: Confluence with less ceremony and a Docker bill

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, comments, and history in PostgreSQL; jobs/cache in Redis; attachments in a persistent local volume by default or S3/Azure Blob
facts.gapVsPaid: It is simpler and faster, but has fewer enterprise macros, workflow controls, templates, marketplace integrations and Jira-native connections than Confluence.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, a strong APP_SECRET, database credentials, persistent volumes, and normally a domain, TLS reverse proxy, and SMTP

alternatives.name: BookStack
alternatives.desc: A wiki organized like a bookshelf; gloriously opinionated and much less flexible than Confluence

facts.install: Fresh Ubuntu install script or manual PHP/MySQL setup
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, permissions, and settings in MySQL/MariaDB; uploaded images and files in the server filesystem or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its compulsory shelf/book/chapter structure and smaller extension surface are far less flexible than Confluence spaces, macros, databases, whiteboards and Jira-connected workflows.
facts.setupBlocker: The official script expects a fresh Ubuntu host; manual installs require PHP extensions, a database, writable storage, mail, and TLS

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.desc: A modern wiki with enough knobs to remind you that you are now the administrator

facts.install: Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, or a Node.js package plus a supported database
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, authentication data, and history in the configured database; optional storage modules can mirror content and assets to Git, local disk, or cloud storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Confluence's mature enterprise templates, macros, whiteboards, marketplace and Atlassian integrations, while shifting hosting and upgrades to you.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision a database and persistent volumes, then configure backups and a TLS reverse proxy for public use

rejectedAlternatives.name: AppFlowy
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The app is open-source, but the official free self-hosted collaboration tier is one seat plus guests

rejectedAlternatives.name: Outline
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A favourite self-hosted wiki recommendation; on-prem now starts at $10 a month and cloud is a 30-day trial

notes: Credibility row: Confluence survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Confluence; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a single-user team documentation workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large integration catalog; mobile capture and notifications; real-time multiplayer.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
